The six multiprocess rows: `cd packages/envoy && . /legion/harness/env.sh && go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -timeout 30m ./cmd/dispatch` → `ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/cmd/dispatch 267.121s`, all six green (TestALiveStreamOnOneProcessCarriesTheOtherProcessesEvent 10.23s, TestTheOutboxPublishesEachEventOnceAcrossBothProcesses 13.27s, TestOneProcessBindsEachDeliveryDurableAndTheOtherStandsBy 12.21s, TestADocumentWriteOnOneProcessClosesTheStaleRoomOnTheOther 10.67s, TestEachLeasedMaintenanceLoopRunsOnceAcrossBothProcesses 70.80s, TestASessionMintedOnOneProcessAuthenticatesOnTheOtherUnderOneSigningKey 15.64s). The reader-facing half: `bash /legion/harness/e2e.sh e2e/inbox.e2e.ts e2e/attention.e2e.ts e2e/doc.e2e.ts e2e/agent-view.e2e.ts e2e/agents.e2e.ts --project=chromium --reporter=line` → `83 passed (5.7m)`, 4 skipped, the implementer's counts reproduced rather than inherited. The document-cursor races at the implementer's own standard of five consecutive runs: `go test -count=5 -timeout 1800s -run 'Room|ColdWrite|UpdateObserver' ./internal/dispatch/docs/` → `ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs 990.306s`, 84 tests × 5, all thirteen stale-room rows and TestTheUpdateObserverNeverRendersAWriteHalfWay among them. The documentation row was checked claim by claim against the code, with its own negative control driven (below). The proof is verified; the failure below is a criterion the proof never covered, not a row of it that does not hold.
implementerProof.whatTheProofDidNotCover: Every leased-loop row of the implementer's proof forces the two passes to overlap — a transaction holding `refs` and `write_suggestions`, and the GitHub fake holding its first deliveries listing. That is a true test of mutual exclusion and it passes. It is not a test of the period: with the overlap removed, the second process runs the same pass again (failure 1).

failures.criterion: Acceptance 1, third clause: "each background loop behaving as the plan's table says - leased so it runs once overall". The plan's §6.2 table leases six loops, giving "N× GitHub rate limit" for architecture-import and delivery-reconcile, "N× waste" for document-compaction, and "N processes write the same excerpts" for reference-excerpts.
failures.evidence: duty.Exclusive (internal/dispatch/duty/exclusive.go:62-85) excludes concurrent passes alone: it takes the lease, runs the pass and gives the lease back, and nothing records that a pass has been made for this period. Two processes whose ticks do not coincide therefore each run the whole pass. That is the ordinary shape, not an edge: duty.RunJittered (duty/ticker.go:22) draws a random phase once at boot and then ticks at a fixed interval, so two processes keep tickers of their own phase, and a rolling update starts the second process minutes after the first. Driven on two real envoy-dispatch processes in this pod against one Postgres 17 and one nats-server 2.10, with the second process started only after the first had finished a pass and released the lease, on the webhook redelivery sweep, whose every pass lists the App webhook's failed deliveries from GitHub before it writes anything — the cost redeliver/sweep.go:226-229 says the lease exists to pay once ("N processes sweeping is N times those list calls for one result"). Observed at head 6f23bd8a: `webhook-redelivery: A ran 1 skipped 0, B ran 1 skipped 0`, and the loopback GitHub counted 2 delivery listings for one sweep window where the first process alone made 1. The same mechanism carries every one of the six leases. Three standing claims are falsified with it: the plan's §6.2 table, redeliver/sweep.go's lease comment, and packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/README.md's "Running more than one process" paragraph, which tells an operator "one process runs the pass and the other logs a skip". Pinned by the red test TestALeasedLoopRunsOnceAcrossAStaggeredStart in packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/multiprocess_test.go (commit 3b3fb04ed2e2, the dispatch-multiprocess CI job), which fails on both halves at this head: `go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -run TestALeasedLoopRunsOnceAcrossAStaggeredStart ./cmd/dispatch` → `the webhook-redelivery pass ran 2 times across the two processes; one process alone would have run it once` and `the two processes listed the webhook's deliveries 2 times for one sweep window`. The architect decided the mechanism changes rather than the wording (Envoy 8f0dcb34ab062d81767d87f9ed42c5b8), preferring a recorded last-completed-pass over a leadership lease and leaving the shape to the implementer; both tests stay, the forced-overlap row for exclusion and this one for the period.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 1: two envoy-dispatch processes against one database and one message bus — no durable bind error, and the standby takes the durable over when its holder stops. Driven at three processes, and with the graceful stop a rolling update actually sends.
proof.surface: Three real envoy-dispatch binaries on one Postgres 17 (pgvector, UTF8/ICU) and one nats-server 2.10 with JetStream, in this issue's pod; driven over HTTP, the processes' own logs and NATS's own ConsumerInfo.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && . /legion/harness/env.sh && go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -timeout 25m -run 'TestProbeThreeProcessesStandByAndPublishEachEventOnce|TestProbeAGracefulStopHandsTheDurableToTheStandby' ./cmd/dispatch   (throwaway probes, removed before this handoff)
proof.observed: Three processes: exactly one logged `NATS consumer bound` for each of delivery-events and delivery-jobs with ConsumerInfo.PushBound true, the other two logged the standby line and no `level=ERROR dispatch delivery:` line at all. Graceful stop: SIGTERM to the holder of delivery-events, the holder exited, and the standby logged `NATS consumer bound` 2.2 s after the signal — the implementer's own row kills with SIGKILL, and SIGTERM is what a roll sends.
proof.negativeControl: The bind refusal is the control and it is observed rather than inferred: the two standby processes are refused the durable by NATS and bind nothing while the holder lives, and the row fails if either of them binds (`both processes bound <durable>, which admits one subscriber`) or logs the bind at ERROR. The hand-over half is its own control in reverse: before the stop the standby holds nothing.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 1: each outbox message meets its per-lane guarantee — every events row reaches published_at once, and the unguarded core-NATS role lane carries each event exactly once — with three outboxes scanning one table rather than two.
proof.surface: The same three processes; comments written alternately through all three processes' HTTP APIs, read back from Postgres, from a core-NATS subscriber on the role subject, and from the JetStream stream by sequence.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && . /legion/harness/env.sh && go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -run TestProbeThreeProcessesStandByAndPublishEachEventOnce ./cmd/dispatch   (throwaway probe, removed before this handoff)
proof.observed: Every claimable events row reached published_at; the role lane notifications.role.probe-three carried exactly one message per source_event_id over twelve comments written round-robin through A, B and C; and each (dedupe key, topic) appeared exactly once in the stream past the pre-write head.
proof.negativeControl: The role lane is the control by construction — core NATS with no nats.MsgId, so nothing dedupes it; without the claim every scanning process selects the same rows and the per-event count is the number of processes. The claim's own refusal shape is `for update skip locked`, which is what makes the other processes' scans skip rather than wait.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 2: a live stream open on one process receives an event committed on the other without the reader reconnecting, and survives the event log being reset beneath it.
proof.surface: Two real envoy-dispatch processes; GET /api/v1/events held open on process A over one HTTP connection while issues are created through process B's API, with `truncate table events restart identity cascade` run against the shared database beneath the open connection.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && . /legion/harness/env.sh && go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -run TestProbeTheLiveStreamRecoversWhenTheEventLogIsReset ./cmd/dispatch   (throwaway probe, removed before this handoff)
proof.observed: B's issue.created arrived on the connection A already held, with no reconnect. After the truncate and a further create through B, A logged `dispatch: the event log was reset; the live stream moved its cursor and ended its open streams` and ended the open stream rather than falling silent; a reader that reconnected was live again on the refilled log and carried the next issue B created.
proof.negativeControl: The reset itself is the deliberately broken input: the refilled log's ids restart at 1, far below the relay's cursor, so `id > cursor` matches nothing and a relay that kept only a cursor is silent for every reader for ever — which is what CI's browser suite caught at 4e8d2e6f. The row fails if the stream merely goes quiet instead of ending. No production path deletes event rows (no `delete from events` outside tests), so the detection cannot fire spuriously on a prune.
proof.note: The implementer's own row covers the cross-process half; this one adds the reset, driven rather than inherited from the browser suite.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 2: the durable gate makes the per-process live room safe — no version, settlement or ask retraction from a stale room, and no edit lost whichever process took it.
proof.surface: Two real envoy-dispatch processes with a real document websocket client holding the room on A, and sixteen concurrent POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/edits split between A and B against that one document; plus the docs package's own stale-room suite.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && . /legion/harness/env.sh && go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -run TestProbeConcurrentDocumentEditsFromBothProcessesLoseNothing ./cmd/dispatch (throwaway probe, removed) && go test -count=5 -timeout 1800s -run 'Room|ColdWrite|UpdateObserver' ./internal/dispatch/docs/
proof.observed: 0 of 16 concurrent edits were refused — no 503 reached an API caller, the stale-room writes taking the cold path as the plan requires — and every one of the sixteen edits was in the stored document read back through both processes' GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/text. The docs suite's 84 matching tests, all thirteen stale-room rows and TestTheUpdateObserverNeverRendersAWriteHalfWay among them, were green five consecutive times: `ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs 990.306s`.
proof.negativeControl: The refusal the gate exists for is driven in the suite rather than assumed: each stale-room row makes the same write with the other process's room current and asserts it succeeds, so what is refused is the staleness and not the write. The concurrency probe is the control in the other direction — a gate that over-reached into healthy rooms would refuse one of the sixteen edits with ErrRoomBehindHead's 503, and none was refused.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 3: the migration rule exists in the repository's own guidance on a branch a contributor branching from main reads.
proof.surface: The repository's own documents at this head, each claim read against the code it cites, and the server's own boot for the placement claim.
proof.command: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && jj diff --git --from 'fork_point(main@origin | @-)' --to @- -- packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/README.md packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/AGENTS.md packages/envoy/deploy/README.md packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/README.md docs/site/src/content/docs/dispatch/running-dispatch.md packages/envoy/AGENTS.md
proof.observed: The expand-then-contract rule with its named stop-the-world exception is in cmd/dispatch/README.md ("Database migrations"), repeated beside the migrations directory in the new internal/dispatch/store/README.md, pointed at from cmd/dispatch/AGENTS.md, and published in running-dispatch.md; 0113's instruction is rescoped to 0113, deploy/README.md's "two releases never serve together" is scoped to the compose deployment, and no document still forbids a rolling update. Each claim I checked holds against the code: pgmigrate.Load refuses an unnamed file (pgmigrate/set.go:103-107), store.migrate reads only the versions it has not recorded so nothing refuses a newer schema (store/store.go:91-108), and the README's "six periodic maintenance loops take a lease" matches the six periodic duty.Exclusive call sites, the seventh being the delivery consumers' bind-poll reconciliation.
proof.negativeControl: Driven, not quoted: a README.md was placed in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/migrations/, envoy-dispatch built from it, and that binary run against a scratch database — boot refused with `migrations refused, none applied: README.md is not named <version>_<name>.up.sql, <version>_<name>.down.sql or <version>_<name>.census.sql, so no runner would apply it` and served nothing. That is why the rule's brief copy sits beside the directory rather than in it. The file was removed before the build was discarded; the workspace never carried it into a commit.
